Test Purpose: Test basic CGM-to-CGM link, from a Application Structure with 'linkuri' APS Attribute within the CGM, to a whole, 1-picture CGM file, with no behaviors or fragments associated with the link.

At the start of the test, the right-hand frame should display a CGM containing a simple picture with a green-filled square on the left and a blue-filled circle on the right, both with thick black borders. The square is within an Application Structure, with id value of "myObjId", and containing a single APS Attribute of type 'linkuri', whose first parameter points to a local CGM file, and whose 2nd and 3rd parameters are null.

To execute the hyperlink, move the mouse anywhere over the square and click the left mouse button. Because there is no "picture behavior" on the link-bearing object in the CGM instance, correct viewer handling of the link will result in picture of the target CGM file replacing the CGM picture in the right-hand frame. This is the default WebCGM picture behavior. You should be able to use the browser "Back" and "Forward" buttons to go back and forth between the target CGM picture and the source CGM picture in the right-hand frame. Note, however, that this latter normal browser behavior is not part of the WebCGM standard, and it is not a pass/fail criterion for WebCGM viewers for this test.

Viewers are required to give visual feedback to the user that a successful pick has occurred, and an indication of the particular object which has been picked. The exact method of feedback is viewer dependent.

The initial view in the left-hand frame is a PNG reference image of the target CGM picture which should appear in the right-hand frame upon activating the link in the WebCGM source instance. There should be no significant visual deviation between the reference image of the left frame and the view in the right frame after link activation.

Caveat: Production problems have caused the reference images of this Release 1.0 to show inaccurate text extents in some labels and in the legend box. Text size/extent should NOT be considered as a verdict criterion of these dynamic tests of this test suite release.
